definition_en: to refuse to accept an offer, an idea, or a person; to turn down an application officially; to attack a transplanted organ; a thing thrown out as imperfect
core_image: 一份申请被推回桌边，上面盖着红色的退回章
scene: 窗口里的工作人员看了一眼材料，盖章后把它推回桌边。The committee rejected the plan without discussion.
sceneCN: 这里 rejected 是 reject 的过去式，取「否决」（第 2 个义项：正式驳回一项提议）；句意为委员会未经讨论就否决了这个方案。画面里可留意：被推回的材料、红色的退回章。

senses.title: To refuse to accept
senses.definition: to say no to something offered or proposed
senses.definitionCN: 对提供或提议之物说不
senses.example: She rejected the job because it meant moving abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 她拒绝了这份工作，因为那意味着要移居国外。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to throw back: an offer is cast back to the hand that held it out.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「扔回去」：提议被抛回伸出它的那只手。

senses.title: To turn down officially
senses.definition: to refuse an application, a plan, or a proposal through a formal decision
senses.definitionCN: 通过正式决定驳回申请、计划或提案
senses.example: The committee rejected the plan without discussion.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会未经讨论就否决了这个方案。
senses.why: A formal no is still a throwing back, but now the throw is made on behalf of an office and recorded.
senses.whyCN: 正式的「不」仍是扔回去，只是这一扔代表一个机构，并被记录下来。

senses.title: To attack transplanted tissue
senses.definition: of a body, to refuse to accept transplanted tissue and attack it
senses.definitionCN: 指身体不接受移植组织并加以攻击
senses.example: Her body rejected the new kidney within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 她的身体在一周内就排斥了新的肾脏。
senses.why: The body throws back what it does not recognise as its own, which is the same gesture at the scale of cells.
senses.whyCN: 身体把不认作自身的东西扔回去，这是同一动作在细胞尺度上的表现。

intro.en: Reject is a throwing back: the Latin verb joins a prefix of return to the verb to throw.
intro.cn: reject 是「扔回去」：这个拉丁动词把表返回的前缀接在「投掷」动词上。

items.en: Iacere meant to throw or cast, and it underlies many English verbs of sending.
items.cn: iacere 意为投掷或抛出，是许多英语「送出」类动词的基础。

items.en: Reicere joined re-, back, with iacere and meant to throw back or cast off.
items.cn: reicere 由 re-（往回）与 iacere 组成，意为扔回去或抛开。

items.en: The participle reiectus meant thrown back, and it gave the noun and the adjective their shape.
items.cn: 分词 reiectus 意为被扔回的，名词与形容词的形式都由此而来。

items.en: French rejecter meant to refuse or cast aside, and English borrowed it in that sense.
items.cn: 法语 rejecter 意为拒绝或抛开，英语即以此义借入。

items.en: Modern medicine applied the word to a body casting off transplanted tissue.
items.cn: 现代医学把这个词用于身体排除移植组织的现象。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs built on the Latin verb to throw; the near-meaning group gathers words for refusing.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁「投掷」动词构成的动词；近义组收表示拒绝的词。

normalIntro.en: The word is a throw: an offer, a plan, or a piece of tissue is sent back where it came from.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一次投掷：提议、方案或一块组织，被送回它来的地方。

normal.en: Re plus iacere, back plus throw: to throw an offer back.
normal.cn: re 加 iacere，往回加扔：把提议扔回去。

normal.en: A committee rejects a plan with a vote, not a shrug.
normal.cn: 委员会用投票否决方案，而不是耸耸肩。

normal.en: A body rejects a transplant because it reads it as foreign.
normal.cn: 身体排斥移植器官，因为它把那读作异物。

normal.en: Rejection is the noun, and it hurts more than the verb.
normal.cn: rejection 是名词，它比动词更伤人。

normal.en: Do not confuse reject with eject, which throws something out for good.
normal.cn: 别把 reject 与 eject 弄混，后者是把东西彻底抛出。

abstract.en: To reject an idea is not to have heard it.
abstract.cn: 否决一个想法，并不等于听懂了它。

abstract.en: Every rejection is a decision about what a group will not become.
abstract.cn: 每一次拒绝，都是一个群体关于「不成为什么」的决定。

abstract.en: A body that rejects a gift is only protecting its own outline.
abstract.cn: 排斥外来物的身体，只是在守住自己的轮廓。

examples.cn: 她的身体在一周内就排斥了新的肾脏。

definition_en: to show or see a connection between things; to tell a story or an account; to feel that you understand someone
core_image: 两条看似无关的旧照片被并排放在桌上
scene: 桌上并排摆着两张旧照片，拍摄年份相差很远。She could not relate the two events until she saw the dates.
sceneCN: 这里 relate 是「把……联系起来」（第 1 个义项：看出或说明事物之间的关联）；句意为她看到日期之后才把这两件事联系起来。画面里可留意：并排的旧照片、上面的年份。

senses.title: To see a connection
senses.definition: to show or understand how two things are connected
senses.definitionCN: 说明或理解两件事如何关联
senses.example: She could not relate the two events until she saw the dates.
senses.exampleCN: 她看到日期之后才把这两件事联系起来。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to carry back, and a connection is made when one fact is carried back to another and set beside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「带回」，而关联正是在把一个事实带回另一个事实、并排放置时形成的。

senses.title: To tell an account
senses.definition: to give an account of events in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 用口头或书面叙述事件的经过
senses.example: He related the whole journey as if it had happened to someone else.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲述整段旅程，仿佛那是发生在别人身上的事。
senses.why: Telling is also a carrying back: the events are brought from memory into the present and handed to a listener.
senses.whyCN: 讲述同样是「带回」：事件从记忆被带到现在，交到听者手里。

senses.title: To feel understood
senses.definition: to feel that you share an experience with someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 感到自己与某人或某物有共同的经历
senses.example: Teenagers relate to songs that name exactly what they feel.
senses.exampleCN: 青少年会对那些准确说出他们感受的歌产生共鸣。
senses.why: When a story is carried back into your own life, you relate to it; the connection is now inside you.
senses.whyCN: 当一个故事被带回你自己的生活，你就对它产生共鸣；此时这条联系在你心里。

intro.en: Relate belongs to the Latin verb to carry: the same stem that gives refer and reference also gives relation and relative.
intro.cn: relate 属于拉丁语表「携带」的动词：给出 refer 与 reference 的同一词干，也给出 relation 与 relative。

items.en: Ferre meant to carry or bear, and it underlies a whole family of verbs of transfer.
items.cn: ferre 意为携带或承载，是整族表转移的动词的基础。

items.en: Referre joined re-, back, with ferre and meant to carry back or report.
items.cn: referre 由 re-（往回）与 ferre 组成，意为带回或报告。

items.en: The supine relatus, carried back, supplied the stem rel- to the later verbs and nouns.
items.cn: 动名词形式 relatus（被带回的）为后来的动词与名词提供了 rel- 词干。

items.en: French relater meant to recount or tell, and English took the verb in that sense first.
items.cn: 法语 relater 意为叙述或讲述，英语先以这个意义借入动词。

items.en: The sense of connecting two things grew from the idea of setting one account beside another.
items.cn: 「把两件事联系起来」这一义，由「把一份叙述放在另一份旁边」的观念发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same carrying family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of connecting and recounting.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「携带」词族的词；近义组收表示联系与叙述的动词。

normalIntro.en: The word carries one thing back to another: two facts side by side, a story to a listener, or a song to your own life.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把一物带回另一物：两个事实并排，一个故事交给听者，或一首歌带回你自己的生活。

normal.en: Re plus late, back plus carried: to carry one thing back to another.
normal.cn: re 加 late（携带）：把一物带回另一物。

normal.en: Relate to a subject means to see yourself in it.
normal.cn: relate to 一个话题，指在其中看到自己。

normal.en: Be related to can mean connected by blood or by cause.
normal.cn: be related to 既可指有血缘，也可指有因果。

normal.en: To relate a story is to tell it from beginning to end.
normal.cn: relate a story 指从头到尾讲述它。

normal.en: Relation, relationship, and relative all come from the same carried stem.
normal.cn: relation、relationship、relative 都出自同一个「携带」词干。

abstract.en: To relate is to refuse to let a fact stand alone.
abstract.cn: 联系，就是不让一个事实孤立地站着。

abstract.en: We relate to stories that carry our own lives back to us.
abstract.cn: 我们与那些把我们自己的生活带回给我们的故事共鸣。

abstract.en: A mind that relates well is a mind with many bridges.
abstract.cn: 善于联系的心，是一座桥很多的城。

examples.cn: 她看到日期之后才把这两件事联系起来。

examples.en: He related the whole journey as if it had happened to someone else.
examples.cn: 他讲述整段旅程，仿佛那是发生在别人身上的事。

examples.en: Teenagers relate to songs that name exactly what they feel.
examples.cn: 青少年会对那些准确说出他们感受的歌产生共鸣。

root: 拉丁 ferre（携带）→ referre（带回、报告）→ relatus（被带回的）→ 法语 relater（叙述）→ 英语 relate；同族有 relation、relationship、relative、relatively，形近的 refer、reference 也出 ferre。

definition_en: a connection between two or more things; a member of one's family; the way people or countries deal with each other
core_image: 家谱图上两条分支在同一个名字处交汇
scene: 摊开的家谱图上，两条支线在同一个名字处交汇。There is no relation between the two numbers.
sceneCN: 这里 relation 是「关联」（第 1 个义项：事物之间的联系）；句意为这两个数字之间没有关联。画面里可留意：家谱图上交汇的两条支线。

senses.title: A connection between things
senses.definition: the way two or more things are connected or affect each other
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多个事物相互连接或影响的方式
senses.example: There is no relation between the two numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个数字之间没有关联。
senses.why: The noun names what is produced when one thing is carried back to another: a line drawn between them.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名「把一物带回另一物」时产生的东西：两者之间画出的一条线。

senses.title: A family member
senses.definition: a person connected to another by blood or marriage
senses.definitionCN: 因血缘或婚姻而与另一人相连的人
senses.example: She is a distant relation of the old painter.
senses.exampleCN: 她是那位老画家的远亲。
senses.why: Kinship is the oldest form of connection, so the word for a link also names the people joined by it.
senses.whyCN: 血缘是最古老的连接形式，因此表「联系」的词也用来指被这条线连起来的人。

senses.title: Official dealings
senses.definition: the way groups or countries deal with one another, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 团体或国家之间往来的方式，通常用复数
senses.example: The two countries restored diplomatic relations after ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 两国在十年之后恢复了外交关系。
senses.why: States also stand in relation to each other, and the plural names the whole web of those dealings.
senses.whyCN: 国家之间也彼此处于关系之中，复数形式便命名这整张往来之网。

intro.en: Relation is the noun of relate, and like refer it comes from the Latin verb of carrying back.
intro.cn: relation 是 relate 的名词，与 refer 一样出自拉丁语表「带回」的动词。

items.en: Referre meant to carry back and to report, built on ferre, to carry.
items.cn: referre 意为带回与报告，由 ferre（携带）构成。

items.en: Relatio named a bringing back, and Latin writers used it for a report to a body and for a logical connection.
items.cn: relatio 指一种带回，拉丁作家用它表示向机构作报告，也表示逻辑上的关联。

items.en: Old French relacion carried the sense of a report and of a connection between things.
items.cn: 古法语 relacion 兼具「报告」与「事物之间关联」两义。

items.en: English extended the noun to people connected by blood, since kinship is a relation in the plainest sense.
items.cn: 英语把这个名词扩展到有血缘的人，因为亲属是最直白的一种关系。

items.en: In the plural, relations came to name the official dealings between states and groups.
items.cn: 在复数形式中，relations 用来指国家与团体之间的正式往来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns of the same carrying family; the near-meaning group gathers words for connection and kinship.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「携带」词族的名词；近义组收表示联系与亲属的词。

normal.en: Relate is the act, relation is the line it draws.

normal.en: Public relations is the work of managing how people see you.

abstract.en: A relation is not a thing but a line between things.
abstract.cn: 关系不是一个东西，而是东西之间的一条线。

abstract.en: Every relation changes both sides a little.
abstract.cn: 每一种关系都会稍稍改变双方。

abstract.en: To bear no relation to something is to share no line with it.
abstract.cn: 与某物毫无关系，就是与它不共用任何一条线。

definition_en: the way two people or groups deal with each other over time; a connection between two things; a romantic partnership
core_image: 两把旧椅子被摆得很近，中间的地面已经磨得发亮
scene: 靠窗摆着两把旧椅子，中间那块地板被来回走动磨得发亮。They built a working relationship over ten years.
sceneCN: 这里 relationship 是「关系」（第 1 个义项：人与人之间长期相处的方式）；句意为他们在十年间建立起一种工作关系。画面里可留意：靠得很近的两把椅子、磨亮的地板。

senses.title: A connection between people
senses.definition: the way two people or groups behave toward each other over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 两个人或群体在一段时间里彼此相处的方式
senses.example: They built a working relationship over ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在十年间建立起一种工作关系。
senses.why: The suffix -ship turns a relation into a continuing state, so the word names something kept up over time rather than a single link.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ship 把 relation 变成一种持续的状态，因此这个词指的是长期维持的东西，而不是一次性的连接。

senses.title: A connection between things
senses.definition: the way two facts, amounts, or ideas are connected
senses.definitionCN: 两个事实、数量或观念相互联系的方式
senses.example: Researchers found a relationship between sleep and memory.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者发现睡眠与记忆之间存在关联。
senses.why: Things, like people, can be set beside each other, and the line between them is also called a relationship.
senses.whyCN: 事物和人一样可以被并置，而它们之间的那条线也叫 relationship。

senses.title: A romantic partnership
senses.definition: a close personal connection in which two people love each other
senses.definitionCN: 两人彼此相爱的一种亲密关系
senses.example: They were in a relationship for three years before they married.
senses.exampleCN: 他们恋爱三年后才结婚。
senses.why: When the personal connection is the closest kind, the general word is used without any further qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 当这种私人联系是最亲密的一种时，这个泛称就不再加任何限定词。

intro.en: Relationship is relation plus the old English suffix of state: a link that is kept going, not a link merely drawn.
intro.cn: relationship 是 relation 加上古英语表状态的后缀：一条被持续维持的线，而不是仅仅画出的线。

items.en: Relatio meant a bringing back and a connection between things.
items.cn: relatio 意为带回，以及事物之间的关联。

items.en: English relation named a connection, a report, and a kinsman.
items.cn: 英语 relation 指关联、报告与亲属。

items.en: The Old English suffix -ship means a state or a condition, as in friendship and hardship.
items.cn: 古英语后缀 -ship 意为状态或境况，如 friendship 与 hardship。

items.en: Putting -ship on relation produced a word for a connection that lasts and is maintained.
items.cn: 把 -ship 加在 relation 上，造出了表示持久且被维系的关系的词。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word became the ordinary term for a couple's partnership.
items.cn: 在二十世纪，这个词成为指伴侣关系的日常说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same connection family; the near-meaning group gathers words for ties and partnerships.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「联系」词族的词；近义组收表示纽带与伴侣关系的词。

entries.definition: A connection or a relative.
A member of one's family.
Compared with something else.

A strong feeling that ties people.

normalIntro.en: The word is a relation with a duration: something two sides keep up, day after day.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是有时间长度的 relation：双方一天天维持下去的东西。

normal.en: Relation plus ship: a relation that is kept like a ship at sea.
normal.cn: relation 加 ship：像船在海上一样被维持的 relation。

normal.en: A working relationship is built, not found.
normal.cn: a working relationship 是建起来的，不是捡到的。

normal.en: A relationship between figures is a pattern, not a person.
normal.cn: 数字之间的关系是一种模式，不是人。

normal.en: In a relationship means the couple is committed.
normal.cn: in a relationship 指两人已经在交往。

normal.en: The ship in relationship is a suffix of state, not a boat.
normal.cn: relationship 里的 ship 是表状态的后缀，不是船。

abstract.en: A relationship is a bridge that both ends must repair.
abstract.cn: 关系是一座两端都得修桥的桥。

abstract.en: What is not maintained quietly returns to being two strangers.
abstract.cn: 不维系的东西，会悄悄退回成两个陌生人。

abstract.en: The quality of a life is largely the quality of its relationships.
abstract.cn: 生活的质地，很大程度上是关系的质地。

examples.en: They built a working relationship over ten years.
examples.cn: 他们在十年间建立起一种工作关系。

examples.en: Researchers found a relationship between sleep and memory.
examples.cn: 研究者发现睡眠与记忆之间存在关联。

examples.en: They were in a relationship for three years before they married.
examples.cn: 他们恋爱三年后才结婚。

dict_mnemonic.text: relation（关系）加 ship（状态）：不是画一条线，而是长期维持这种状态，就是 relationship。

root: 拉丁 relatio（带回、关联）→ 英语 relation ＋ 古英语后缀 -ship（状态）→ relationship；同族有 relate、relation、relative、related，词干出自拉丁 ferre（携带）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a link that is kept up; the senses move from a personal connection over time, to a pattern between facts, to a couple's partnership.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被持续维持的线」；义项从长期的人际联系，到事实之间的模式，再到伴侣关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two old chairs set close together, the floor between them worn bright.
core.cn: 核心意象：两把旧椅子被摆得很近，中间的地面已经磨得发亮。

branches.cn: 十年并肩工作

branches.cn: 同一张图上的睡眠与记忆

branches.en: three years before a wedding
branches.cn: 婚礼之前的三年

branches.en: a partnership at work and at home
branches.cn: 工作与家庭中的同一种相伴

branches.en: a pattern between facts and a pattern between people
branches.cn: 事实之间的模式与人之间的模式

intro.cn: 表联系的名词接上古英语表状态的后缀，合成词便命名一条延续于时间中的线。

latinIntro.cn: 词干是 relatio（带回、关联）；-ship 是英语表状态的后缀。

definition_en: true only when compared with something else; connected with a particular subject; a member of one's family
core_image: 两个人站在不同高度的台阶上比身高
scene: 两个人站在不同高度的台阶上，看起来竟一样高。Happiness is relative to what a person expects.
sceneCN: 这里 relative 是「相对的」（第 1 个义项：只有在比较中才成立）；句意为幸福相对于一个人的期待而言。画面里可留意：不同高度的台阶、看起来一样高的两人。

senses.title: True only by comparison
senses.definition: not absolute, but true when measured against something else
senses.definitionCN: 非绝对的，只有在与其他事物比较时才成立
senses.example: Happiness is relative to what a person expects.
senses.exampleCN: 幸福相对于一个人的期待而言。
senses.why: The Latin participle means carried back, and a value carried back to another value is measured by it rather than in itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁分词意为「被带回的」，一个数值被带回另一个数值那里，就是以它为准来衡量，而不是就自身而言。

senses.title: Connected with a subject
senses.definition: having a connection with a particular matter
senses.definitionCN: 与某个特定事项有关联
senses.example: The report gathers the facts relative to the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告汇集了与那场事故相关的事实。
senses.why: Something carried back to a question is relevant to it, and the same adjective names that connection.
senses.whyCN: 被带回到某个问题那里的东西就与它有关，同一个形容词命名这种关联。

senses.title: A family member
senses.definition: a person connected to another by blood or marriage
senses.definitionCN: 因血缘或婚姻而与另一人相连的人
senses.example: A distant relative left her the old house.
senses.exampleCN: 一位远亲把那座老房子留给了她。
senses.why: Persons related by blood are quite literally carried back to a common ancestor, and the adjective became a noun for them.
senses.whyCN: 有血缘的人确实可以被带回同一个祖先，于是这个形容词就成了指他们的名词。

intro.en: Relative is the adjective of the Latin participle carried back; what is carried back is measured against something else, or joined to a family.
intro.cn: relative 是拉丁分词「被带回的」所对应的形容词；被带回的东西，要么以别物为尺，要么归入一个家族。

items.en: Ferre meant to carry, the root of referre and of the whole rel- family.
items.cn: ferre 意为携带，是 referre 与整个 rel- 词族的根。

items.en: Relatus, the participle of referre, meant carried back or having reference to.
items.cn: relatus 是 referre 的分词，意为被带回的或有所指的。

items.en: Relativus meant having relation to something else, the grammatical and philosophical term.
items.cn: relativus 意为与其他事物有关的，是语法与哲学术语。

items.en: English used the adjective for values that hold only in comparison, as opposed to absolute ones.
items.cn: 英语用这个形容词表示只在比较中成立的数值，与「绝对」相对。

items.en: The noun use for a family member grew from the sense of persons referred to one another by blood.
items.cn: 指亲属的名词用法，由「因血缘而彼此相关的人」这一意义发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same carrying stem; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of comparison and kinship words.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「携带」词干的词；近义组收表比较的形容词与亲属词。

entries.definition: In comparison with something else.
The state of being relative.
A connection; a relative.

normalIntro.en: The word means carried back to something else: a value to another value, a fact to a question, a person to a family.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词意为「被带回别处」：数值带回另一数值，事实带回一个问题，人带回一个家族。

normal.en: Relative to means measured against.
normal.cn: relative to 意为以……为参照来衡量。

normal.en: Relative humidity compares moisture with the maximum the air can hold.
normal.cn: relative humidity 把湿度与空气能容纳的最大量相比。

normal.en: A close relative is a near member of the family.
normal.cn: a close relative 是家族中的近亲。

normal.en: Relative importance ranks things against each other.
normal.cn: relative importance 是把事物相互比较后的轻重。

normal.en: Relative and absolute are a pair; one needs the other.
normal.cn: relative 与 absolute 是一对，彼此需要。

abstract.en: Almost everything we call large is only relatively large.
abstract.cn: 我们所说的大，几乎都只是相对地大。

abstract.en: To see things as relative is not to see them as unreal.
abstract.cn: 把事物看作相对的，并不等于把它们看作虚幻的。

abstract.en: A family is the first place where a person is a relative.
abstract.cn: 家庭是一个人最初成为「亲属」的地方。

examples.en: Happiness is relative to what a person expects.
examples.cn: 幸福相对于一个人的期待而言。

examples.en: The report gathers the facts relative to the accident.
examples.cn: 这份报告汇集了与那场事故相关的事实。

examples.en: A distant relative left her the old house.
examples.cn: 一位远亲把那座老房子留给了她。

dict_mnemonic.text: relate（带回、关联）加 ive：必须带回别物才有意义，是相对；与某个问题带回一处，是相关；因血缘被带回一家，是亲戚。

root: 拉丁 ferre（携带）→ referre（带回）→ relatus（被带回的）→ 拉丁 relativus（有关的）→ 英语 relative；同族有 relatively、relativity、relation、relate。

sensesIntro.en: The core is carried back to something else; the senses move from a value measured by comparison, to a fact tied to a subject, to a person tied to a family.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被带回别物那里」；义项从以比较为准的数值，到与某个主题相连的事实，再到与家族相连的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people on steps of different heights, looking the same size.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人站在不同高度的台阶上比身高。

branches.cn: 只有放在一起才有意义的两个数字

branches.en: facts gathered around one accident
branches.cn: 围绕一场事故汇集的材料

branches.en: an old house left by a cousin
branches.cn: 一位远亲留下的老房子

branches.en: a comparison and a reference to a subject
branches.cn: 一次比较与一次对主题的指向

branches.en: tied to a question and tied to a family
branches.cn: 与一个问题相连，与一个家族相连

latinIntro.cn: 词根是 relatus（被带回的）；-ivus 构成形容词 relativus。

definition_en: when compared with other things of the same kind; to a fairly great degree, though not absolutely
core_image: 两只手把同一块石头举到不同高度的背景前比较大小
scene: 同一块石头，放在不同高度的背景前，看上去大小完全不同。The room was relatively cheap for the city centre.
sceneCN: 这里 relatively 是「相对地」（第 1 个义项：与同类事物相比而言）；句意为对市中心来说，这个房间相对便宜。画面里可留意：同一块石头在不同背景下的观感。

senses.title: By comparison
senses.definition: when measured against other things of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 与同类事物相比较而言
senses.example: The room was relatively cheap for the city centre.
senses.exampleCN: 对市中心来说，这个房间相对便宜。
senses.why: The adverb keeps the comparison inside the sentence: cheap compared with other rooms, not cheap in itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词把比较留在句子内部：与别的房间相比便宜，而不是本身就便宜。

senses.title: Fairly, though not absolutely
senses.definition: to a fairly high degree, with the comparison left understood
senses.definitionCN: 达到相当高的程度，而比较对象被省略
senses.example: The work was finished relatively quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 这项工作完成得相当快。
senses.why: When the other term of the comparison is obvious, the word drifts toward a soft form of very.
senses.whyCN: 当比较的另一方显而易见时，这个词就漂向一种柔和的「很」。

intro.en: Relatively is the adverb of relative, and it keeps the comparison that the adjective implies.
intro.cn: relatively 是 relative 的副词，它保留了形容词所暗示的比较。

items.en: Relatus meant carried back, and what is carried back is always measured against something.
items.cn: relatus 意为被带回的，而被带回之物总是以某物为尺。

items.en: Relativus meant having relation to something else.
items.cn: relativus 意为与其他事物有关的。

items.en: English relative described values that hold only in comparison.
items.cn: 英语 relative 描述只在比较中成立的数值。

items.en: The adverb ending -ly turned the comparison into a way of qualifying a statement.
items.cn: 副词词尾 -ly 把这种比较变成限定陈述的方式。

items.en: Modern speech uses the adverb to soften a claim that would be too strong if stated flatly.
items.cn: 现代口语用这个副词来缓冲一个说得太满的论断。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same comparison family; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of degree and comparison.
note.cn: 形近组收同一比较词族的词；近义组收表程度与比较的副词。

entries.definition: Compared, not absolute.
The state of being relative.
A connection.
When compared with others.
To a moderately high degree.
To a certain degree.

normalIntro.en: The adverb warns the reader that a comparison is being made, even when the other side of it stays silent.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词提醒读者：这里正在做比较，即使比较的另一方没有说出口。

normal.en: Relatively cheap means cheap next to the other ones.
normal.cn: relatively cheap 指与别的相比便宜。

normal.en: Relatively speaking is the phrase that makes the comparison explicit.
normal.cn: relatively speaking 是把比较说清楚的那个短语。

normal.en: Relatively few means fewer than you might expect here.
normal.cn: relatively few 指比你在这种情况下预期的要少。

normal.en: The word softens a claim without withdrawing it.
normal.cn: 这个词软化论断，但不撤回论断。

normal.en: Drop the comparison and the sentence may become false.
normal.cn: 去掉比较，这句话可能就不成立了。

abstract.en: Every relative judgement borrows its scale from somewhere.
abstract.cn: 每一个相对判断都从某处借来它的尺度。

abstract.en: Relatively is a small word that keeps us honest about context.
abstract.cn: relatively 这个小词让我们对语境保持诚实。

abstract.en: What is relatively safe may still be unsafe enough.
abstract.cn: 相对安全的东西，也可能仍然足够危险。

examples.en: The room was relatively cheap for the city centre.
examples.cn: 对市中心来说，这个房间相对便宜。

examples.en: The work was finished relatively quickly.
examples.cn: 这项工作完成得相当快。

examples.en: Relatively few students chose the harder course.
examples.cn: 相对较少的学生选了那门更难的课。

dict_mnemonic.text: relative（相对的）加 ly：把「跟谁比」这句话塞进一个副词里，就是「相对地」；比较对象省略时，就成了「相当」。

root: 拉丁 relatus（被带回的）→ relativus（有关的）→ 英语 relative ＋ -ly → relatively；与 relative、relativity、relation 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an implied comparison; the senses move from a comparison that is stated, to a softened degree word when the comparison is understood.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「隐含的比较」；义项从明说的比较，到比较对象被省略时的缓和程度词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one stone shown against backgrounds of different heights, seeming to change size.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手把同一块石头举到不同背景前比较大小。

branches.cn: 在这个地段算低的房租

branches.en: work done faster than expected
branches.cn: 比预期完成得更快的工作

branches.en: a comparison made and a degree implied
branches.cn: 明做的比较与暗示的程度

branches.en: a claim that stops short of very
branches.cn: 没有说到「很」的论断

branches.en: a price judged only against neighbours
branches.cn: 只与邻近房源比较的价格

intro.en: The adjective of comparison takes the English adverb ending, and the result marks a judgement that depends on a scale.
intro.cn: 表比较的形容词接上英语副词词尾，结果便标记一个依赖尺度的判断。

latinIntro.cn: 词干是 relativus（与其他事物有关的）；-ly 是英语副词词尾。

definition_en: to become less tense in body or mind; to make a rule or a limit less strict; to become less tight or less severe
core_image: 一直攥紧的拳头在长椅上慢慢松开
scene: 他在长椅上坐了很久，一直攥紧的拳头才慢慢松开。A hot bath helps her relax after a long shift.
sceneCN: 这里 relax 是「放松」（第 1 个义项：身体或心情由紧张转为松弛）；句意为长时间轮班之后，热水澡能帮她放松。画面里可留意：慢慢松开的拳头、长椅。

senses.title: To become less tense
senses.definition: to let the body or the mind become loose and calm
senses.definitionCN: 让身体或心情变得松弛平静
senses.example: A hot bath helps her relax after a long shift.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间轮班之后，热水澡能帮她放松。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to loosen, and the prefix adds a returning: tension that has tightened is let back to its resting state.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「使松」，前缀则添上「回」的意味：绷紧的张力被放回到休息状态。

senses.title: To make a rule less strict
senses.definition: to make a rule, a limit, or a control less severe
senses.definitionCN: 使规则、限制或管制不那么严格
senses.example: The city relaxed the rules on street markets last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市去年春天放宽了街头集市的规定。
senses.why: A rule can be tight like a muscle, and loosening it is described with the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 规则可以像肌肉一样紧绷，而松开它用的是同一个动词。

senses.title: To become less tight
senses.definition: to become less firm, less intense, or less severe
senses.definitionCN: 变得不那么紧、不那么强烈或不那么严重
senses.example: His grip on the rail relaxed once the ship was steady.
senses.exampleCN: 船稳下来之后，他抓着栏杆的手松了。
senses.why: Here the loosening is physical again, but the object is a hold or a tension rather than a person.
senses.whyCN: 这里的松弛又回到物理层面，只是对象是握力或张力，而不是一个人。

intro.en: Relax is to loosen: the Latin adjective for loose becomes a verb, and the prefix sets the loosening in motion.
intro.cn: relax 意为「使松」：拉丁语表「松」的形容词变成动词，前缀让这一松开得以进行。

items.en: Laxus meant loose, slack, or wide, and it is the root of the whole family.
items.cn: laxus 意为松的、松弛的或宽的，是整个词族的根。

items.en: Laxare meant to loosen, slacken, or let go.
items.cn: laxare 意为放松、使松弛或放开。

items.en: Relaxare added re- and meant to loosen back, to unbend, or to relieve.
items.cn: relaxare 加上 re-，意为松回去、舒展或缓解。

items.en: French relaxer carried the medical sense of easing tension into English.
items.cn: 法语 relaxer 把「缓解紧张」这一医学用法带入英语。

items.en: English widened the verb from muscles and minds to rules, prices, and controls.
items.cn: 英语把这个动词从肌肉与心情扩展到规则、价格与管制。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin adjective for loose; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of resting and easing.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁语表「松」的形容词构成的词；近义组收表示休息与缓解的动词。

normal.en: A relaxed person is one whose shoulders have come down.

normal.en: The adjective relaxing describes what does the loosening.

normal.en: Release and relax are different words; one lets go, one slackens.

abstract.en: To relax is to stop holding what no longer needs holding.
abstract.cn: 放松，就是停止握住已经不必握住的东西。

abstract.en: A mind that never slackens cannot tell what matters.
abstract.cn: 从不松弛的心，分不清什么要紧。

abstract.en: Some rules deserve to be loosened, and some only appear to.
abstract.cn: 有些规则值得放宽，有些只是看起来如此。

examples.en: A hot bath helps her relax after a long shift.
examples.cn: 长时间轮班之后，热水澡能帮她放松。

definition_en: to let a person or a thing go free; to make a film, a record, or a report available to the public; to free someone from a duty or a debt
core_image: 笼门被拉开，一只鸟迟疑了一下才飞出去
scene: 笼门被拉开，里面的鸟迟疑了一下，才振翅飞向树梢。The government will release the report on Monday.
sceneCN: 这里 release 是「发布」（第 2 个义项：把消息或文件公开给公众）；句意为政府将在周一发布这份报告。画面里可留意：被拉开的笼门、飞向树梢的鸟。

senses.title: To let go free
senses.definition: to stop holding a person or an animal and let it go
senses.definitionCN: 不再抓住某人或某动物，任其离开
senses.example: The keeper released the bird at the edge of the wood.
senses.exampleCN: 管理员在林边放飞了那只鸟。
senses.why: The French word behind it means to let go or give back, so the first sense is simply the opening of a hand or a door.
senses.whyCN: 其背后的法语词意为「放开、交还」，所以第一义就是把手或门打开。

senses.title: To make public
senses.definition: to make a film, a record, or a piece of information available to everyone
senses.definitionCN: 让影片、唱片或信息向所有人公开
senses.example: The government will release the report on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 政府将在周一发布这份报告。
senses.why: A work kept from the public is held tight; making it available is the same letting go, applied to information.
senses.whyCN: 被扣住不公开的作品是攥紧的；让它面世就是同一种「放开」，只是对象变成了信息。

senses.title: To free from an obligation
senses.definition: to free someone from a duty, a debt, or a promise
senses.definitionCN: 使某人免于某项义务、债务或承诺
senses.example: The court released him from the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 法院解除了他在这份合同中的义务。
senses.why: To be bound by a duty is to be held, and to be released is to have that hold removed.
senses.whyCN: 被义务束缚就是被抓住，而被解除就是那只手被移开。

intro.en: Release came into English through a French verb meaning to let go or give back; in English it is a separate word from relax, which was borrowed straight from Latin.
intro.cn: release 经由一个意为「放开、交还」的法语动词进入英语；在英语里它与 relax 是两个词，后者直接借自拉丁语。

items.en: Old French laissier meant to let, leave, or let go, and it stands behind the second half of the word.
items.cn: 古法语 laissier 意为让、留下或放开，构成这个词的后半部分。

items.en: Relesser joined re- with laissier and meant to let go, give back, or remit.
items.cn: relesser 由 re- 与 laissier 组合，意为放开、交还或免除。

items.en: The French noun reles named a letting go, a remission of a debt, or a release from custody.
items.cn: 法语名词 reles 指放开、债务的免除或从拘押中释放。

items.en: English borrowed both the verb and the noun, keeping the senses of freeing and remitting.
items.cn: 英语同时借入动词与名词，保留了「释放」与「免除」两义。

items.en: Publishing gave the word its sense of issuing a film, a record, or a statement to the public.
items.cn: 出版业赋予这个词「向公众发行影片、唱片或声明」的意义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that begin like release; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of freeing and issuing.
note.cn: 形近组收与 release 开头相近的词；近义组收表示释放与发行的动词。

scene: 一叠厚厚的材料摊在桌上，他从中抽出几页，放到桌子中央。Only the facts relevant to the case were read aloud.

senses.title: Connected with the matter
senses.definition: directly connected with the subject or the problem at hand
senses.definitionCN: 与手头的话题或问题直接相连
senses.example: Only the facts relevant to the case were read aloud.
senses.exampleCN: 只有与本案相关的事实被朗读出来。
senses.why: The word began as a picture of something lifted up to help, and it now names whatever lifts a discussion forward.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初描绘被举起以提供帮助之物，如今命名一切能推动讨论向前的东西。

senses.title: Useful and to the point
senses.definition: important and useful for the purpose being considered
senses.definitionCN: 对正在考虑的目的而言重要且有用
senses.example: Her question was short but highly relevant to the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 她的问题很短，却与这项决定高度相关。
senses.why: Connection alone is not enough; the thing must also carry weight, which is why relevant often implies useful.
senses.whyCN: 仅有联系还不够，那件事物还必须具有分量，因此 relevant 常隐含「有用」。

intro.en: Relevant comes from a Latin verb meaning to lift up and relieve, not from the carrying verb behind relate; the two families are distinct.
intro.cn: relevant 出自一个意为「举起、减轻」的拉丁动词，而不是 relate 所属的那个「携带」动词；这两个词族彼此不同。

items.en: Relevare joined re- with levare and meant to raise up, relieve, or assist.
items.cn: relevare 由 re- 与 levare 组合，意为举起、减轻或援助。

items.en: The participle relevans, lifting up or helping, named what comes to the aid of a matter.
items.cn: 分词 relevans（举起或帮助）指对某件事物施以援手者。

items.en: French relevant meant depending upon or pertinent, and English took the adjective in that sense.
items.cn: 法语 relevant 意为「取决于」或「切题」，英语即以这个意义借入形容词。

items.en: English narrowed the word to what bears on the question under discussion.
items.cn: 英语把这个词收窄为「与正在讨论的问题有关」。

senses.definitionCN: 疼痛、焦虑或困境结束后所产生的轻松愉快感
senses.example: She felt a huge sense of relief when the exam results finally arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 考试成绩终于公布时，她感到如释重负。
senses.why: The Latin verb relevare means to raise or lift up, so the core image is a weight being lifted off the body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 relevare 表示「抬起、举起」，所以核心画面是压在身上的重物被抬走，紧绷随之松开。

senses.title: Help for people in trouble
senses.definition: money, food, or other help given to people who are in need, especially after a disaster
senses.definitionCN: 给予困境中的人们的钱、食物或其他帮助，尤指灾后援助
senses.example: Relief supplies reached the village two days after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后两天，救援物资运抵了村庄。
senses.why: If the core image is lifting a weight, then lifting people out of hardship naturally gives the word the sense of aid itself.
senses.whyCN: 既然核心画面是把重物抬起，那么把人从苦难中托起来，就自然延伸出「援助」这一义项。

senses.title: A design raised above a surface
senses.definition: a design cut into stone or metal so that it stands out above the flat background
senses.definitionCN: 在石头或金属上雕刻出的、凸出于平面的图案
senses.example: The coin shows the queen's head in relief.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚硬币上铸有女王头像的浮雕。
senses.why: The raised part of a carving is literally lifted above the surface, which matches the lifting image at the heart of the word.
senses.whyCN: 浮雕凸起的部分正是从平面被「抬起来」的，与这个词核心的抬起画面完全吻合。

senses.title: A shift that takes over a duty
senses.definition: a person or group that takes over a job from someone else so that the work can continue
senses.definitionCN: 从他人手中接过工作、使工作中断得以继续的人或班组
senses.example: The night relief arrived at six in the morning.
senses.exampleCN: 夜班接替人员早上六点到了。
senses.why: Passing a load from one pair of shoulders to another is the same lifting picture, applied to work shifts.
senses.whyCN: 把重担从一副肩膀交到另一副肩膀，仍是「抬起并转移」这个画面，用在轮班场景里就成了换班。

intro.en: Relief comes through Old French from the Latin verb relevare, built from the prefix re- and the verb levare.
intro.cn: relief 经由古法语来自拉丁动词 relevare，该词由前缀 re- 与动词 levare 组合而成。

items.en: Relevare means to raise up, lift, or lighten, and is formed from re- plus levare.
items.cn: relevare 意为抬起、举起或减轻，由 re- 与 levare 构成。

items.en: Levare comes from the adjective levis, light in weight, the same root found in levity.
items.cn: levare 源自形容词 levis「重量轻的」，这个词根也见于 levity。

items.en: Relevium names a payment raised from a tenant, showing the idea of something lifted up.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 relevium 指向佃户征收的一笔款项，同样带有「被抬起之物」的意味。

items.en: Old French relief carries the senses of a raising, of help, and of a remainder.
items.cn: 古法语 relief 同时有「抬起」「帮助」「剩余部分」几层意思。

items.en: English borrows the word for help given to someone in trouble and for a raised carving.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词，用于表示给予困境中人的帮助，也指凸起的雕刻。

items.en: Modern English keeps the eased feeling, the aid, the raised carving, and the relieving shift.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了宽慰感、援助、浮雕以及换班这几层含义。

note.en: Relief belongs to a re- and lev- family about lifting weight, and it sits near words for making trouble smaller.
note.cn: relief 属于由 re- 与 lev- 构成、表示「抬起重量」的词族，同时又与表示「使麻烦变小」的词相邻。

entries.definitionCN: 缓解；减轻，是 relief 对应的动词形式

entries.definition: feeling glad that a worry or pain has gone
entries.definitionCN: 感到宽慰的，由 relieve 加 -ed 构成

entries.definition: a lack of seriousness, often in a situation that needs it
entries.definitionCN: 轻浮；轻率，与 relief 共享 levis「轻」的词根

entries.definition: a pleasant feeling of being free from pain or worry
entries.definitionCN: 舒适；安慰，侧重身心放松的状态

entries.definition: the state of feeling no pain, difficulty, or worry
entries.definitionCN: 轻松；安逸，强调没有负担

entries.definition: help, especially money or goods given to people in need
entries.definitionCN: 援助；救助，与 relief 的第二义项接近

normalIntro.en: The word is built on Latin levare, to lift, so the memory hooks mostly involve lifting a weight.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语 levare「举起」之上，所以记忆钩子大多围绕「把重物抬走」。

normal.en: Re- plus lev- gives the picture of lifting something up again, and the weight comes off.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 加词根 lev-，画面是把东西重新抬起来，重量随之离开。

normal.en: Compare elevator: both words lift, one lifts people, the other lifts weight off a mind.
normal.cn: 对比 elevator：两者都在「抬起」，一个载人，一个把重量从心头抬走。

normal.en: The pair relief and relieve differs only by the last letter, noun against verb.
normal.cn: relief 与 relieve 只差最后一个字母，一个是名词，一个是动词。

normal.en: A sigh of relief is literally the sound of a lifted weight.
normal.cn: a sigh of relief 字面上就是重物被抬走时那口长气。

normal.en: Disaster relief is help that lifts a whole town back onto its feet.
normal.cn: disaster relief 是把整座城镇重新托起来的援助。

abstract.en: Imagine a backpack of stones sliding off your back; your shoulders drop and you breathe out.
abstract.cn: 想象一包石头从背上滑落，肩膀塌下来，你长长呼气。

abstract.en: Think of a carved coin: the head is pushed up out of the flat metal.
abstract.cn: 想一枚硬币，头像被从平整的金属里顶出来。

abstract.en: Picture a relay of workers: one steps away, the next takes the load.
abstract.cn: 想象工人接力：一个人退下，下一个人接过重物。

examples.en: She breathed a sigh of relief when she heard the news.
examples.cn: 听到这个消息，她松了一口气。

examples.en: The government sent relief to the flooded region.
examples.cn: 政府向洪涝地区运送了救援物资。

examples.en: The statue is carved in relief on the temple wall.
examples.cn: 庙墙上雕着这座雕像的浮雕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞丽福」——想象瑞丽小城送来福气，紧绷的心一下松开；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再次、向后）+ levare（举起，源自 levis「轻」）构成 relevare（抬起、减轻），经古法语 relief 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: One image of a lifted weight grows into four senses: the eased mind, the aid given, the raised carving, and the shift that takes over.
sensesIntro.cn: 「抬起重量」这一个画面长出四个义项：心里的轻松、给出的援助、凸起的浮雕，以及接过工作的换班。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy weight lifted from the shoulders.
core.cn: 核心意象：压在肩上的重物被抬起搬走。

branches.en: The mind feels the weight go, so relief names the eased feeling.
branches.cn: 心里感到重量消失，于是 relief 指那种松弛下来的感觉。

branches.en: Lifting a person out of hardship becomes the name for the help itself.
branches.cn: 把人从困境中托起来，进一步成为「援助」的名称。

branches.en: A carving stands up above the flat surface, exactly like something lifted.
branches.cn: 浮雕高出平面，正像被抬起的东西。

branches.en: A load passed to fresh hands becomes the relieving shift.
branches.cn: 重担交到新的人手上，就成了接替的班次。

branches.en: Both the eased feeling and the aid come from the same upward movement.
branches.cn: 心中的松弛与外来的援助都源自同一个向上的动作。

intro.en: Relief is built from a Latin prefix and a Latin root, with a French noun ending carried into English.
intro.cn: relief 由拉丁前缀、拉丁词根以及传入英语的法语名词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin prefix re- means back or again, and levare means to lift, so together they describe lifting a burden away.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 表示「向后、再次」，levare 表示「举起」，合起来就是「把重担抬走」。

items.example: The prefix re- returns in relieve and remove.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 也出现在 relieve 与 remove 中。

items.example: The root lev- also appears in elevate and levity.
items.exampleCN: 词根 lev- 也出现在 elevate 与 levity 中。

items.example: Levare is the verb behind relief and relieve.
items.exampleCN: levare 是 relief 与 relieve 背后的动词。

items.example: Levis is the source of the lev- root in this family.
items.exampleCN: levis 是这一词族中 lev- 词根的来源。

items.meaningCN: 表示结果或状态的名词词尾
items.example: The ending -ief carries the French form into English relief.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ief 把法语形式带进了英语 relief。

items.meaning: to lift up again, to ease
items.example: Relevare joins re- and levare into a single verb.
items.exampleCN: relevare 把 re- 与 levare 合成了一个动词。

items.example: Levity uses the same levis root for lightness of behaviour.
items.exampleCN: levity 用同一个 levis 词根表示举止上的轻。

items.example: Alleviate adds ad- to the same levis root.
items.exampleCN: alleviate 在同一个 levis 词根前加了 ad-。

definition_zh: 缓解；减轻；接替；使摆脱；调剂
definition_en: to make pain, worry, or a difficult situation less serious
core_image: 拧得过紧的阀门被慢慢松开，压力随之下降
scene: 护士调慢了输液速度，药物在几分钟内让病人的疼痛明显减轻。The nurse slowed the drip, and the drug began to relieve his pain within minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 relieve 是「缓解」（第 1 个义项：使疼痛或问题变轻）；句意：护士调慢了输液速度，药物在几分钟内开始缓解他的疼痛。

pos.zh: 缓解；减轻；接替；使摆脱；调剂

derivatives.zh: 由动词 relieve 去掉词尾构成，义为「宽慰；救济」
relieve 加 -ed 构成，义为「感到宽慰的」
加否定前缀 un- 与 -ed，义为「未获缓解的」

senses.title: To make pain or trouble less severe
senses.definition: to make a feeling of pain, worry, or pressure weaker or easier to bear
senses.definitionCN: 使疼痛、忧虑或压力的感觉变弱、变得容易承受
senses.example: This medicine will relieve your headache in about half an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药大约半小时后能缓解你的头痛。
senses.why: The Latin source means to lift a weight, so easing pain is pictured as taking part of the load off.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词源意为「抬起重量」，因此缓解疼痛被想象成把部分负担从身上拿走。

senses.title: To take over a duty from someone
senses.definition: to take the place of someone who is on duty so that they can rest
senses.definitionCN: 替换正在值班的人，使其可以休息
senses.example: A fresh guard came to relieve the man at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 一名新哨兵来替换门口的那个人。
senses.why: If a load can be lifted and handed on, then a duty can be lifted from one person and given to another.
senses.whyCN: 既然重物可以抬起并转交，那么职责也能从一个人身上卸下、交给另一个人。

senses.title: To free someone from something unpleasant
senses.definition: to take away a duty, worry, or possession from someone, often formally
senses.definitionCN: 把某项职责、忧虑或财物从某人身上拿走，常用于正式语境
senses.example: Let me relieve you of that heavy bag.
senses.exampleCN: 让我帮你拿那个重包吧。
senses.why: Lifting a weight off a person is the same motion as taking a burden or duty away from them.
senses.whyCN: 把人身上的重量抬走，与替他拿走负担或职务是同一个动作。

senses.title: To add variety to something dull
senses.definition: to make a boring or uniform situation more interesting by adding something different
senses.definitionCN: 通过加入变化，使枯燥或单调的场面变得有趣
senses.example: A few jokes relieved the tension in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 几个笑话缓解了房间里的紧张气氛。
senses.why: Relief is a lifting of pressure, and a dull stretch of time is felt as pressure that a change lifts away.
senses.whyCN: relief 的本质是卸下压力，而漫长的沉闷也像一种压力，变化正是把它抬走。

intro.en: Relieve comes from Old French relever, which descends from the Latin verb relevare.
intro.cn: relieve 来自古法语 relever，后者可追溯到拉丁动词 relevare。

items.en: Relevare combines re- with levare, to lift, and means to raise up or lighten.
items.cn: relevare 由 re- 与 levare「举起」组合，意为抬起或减轻。

items.en: Levare is built on levis, light in weight, which also gives levity.
items.cn: levare 建立在 levis「重量轻」之上，这个词根也产生了 levity。

items.en: Colloquial forms of relevare spread through the spoken language of the late empire.
items.cn: relevare 的口语形式在帝国晚期的日常语言中传播开来。

items.en: Old French relever means to raise again, to help up, and to ease.
items.cn: 古法语 relever 表示重新举起、扶起以及缓解。

items.en: English adopts relieve for easing pain, taking over a duty, and freeing someone of a burden.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪引入 relieve，用于缓解疼痛、接替职责以及替人卸下负担。

items.en: The modern verb keeps all three threads and adds the lighter sense of adding variety.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了这三条线索，并增添了「调剂、增加变化」这层较轻的含义。

note.en: Relieve is the verb behind relief and shares its lifting root with several light-related words.
note.cn: relieve 是名词 relief 背后的动词，并与若干表示「轻」的词共享抬起的词根。

entries.definition: the feeling that comes when pain or worry ends
entries.definitionCN: 宽慰；缓解，是 relieve 对应的名词

entries.definition: glad that a worry or pain has gone
entries.definitionCN: 感到宽慰的，由 relieve 加 -ed 构成

entries.definition: to make pain or suffering less severe
entries.definitionCN: 减轻；缓和，与 relieve 共享 levis 词根，只是前缀不同

entries.definition: to make pain or a problem less severe
entries.definitionCN: 减轻；缓和，语体比 relieve 更轻

entries.definition: to make someone calmer or make pain less sharp
entries.definitionCN: 安抚；使疼痛缓和，强调舒适感

entries.definition: to make a load or a mood less heavy
entries.definitionCN: 减轻；使轻松，保留了「重量」的比喻

normalIntro.en: Relieve is the verb form of the re- and lev- family, so its hooks all circle the idea of lifting.
normalIntro.cn: relieve 是 re- 与 lev- 词族的动词形式，所以记忆钩子都围绕「抬起」。

normal.en: Say the pair together: relief is the state, relieve is the act of bringing it about.
normal.cn: 把这一对一起记：relief 是状态，relieve 是带来这种状态的动作。

normal.en: The root lev- also lifts in elevate and lever, both about raising something.
normal.cn: 词根 lev- 在 elevate 和 lever 里同样表示「抬起」。

normal.en: Relieve someone of a bag means taking the weight into your own hand.
normal.cn: relieve someone of a bag 就是把重量接到自己手里。

normal.en: The past participle relieved doubles as the everyday adjective for feeling better.
normal.cn: 过去分词 relieved 同时也常用作形容词，表示「放心了」。

normal.en: Remember the fixed phrase relieve the pressure when talking about stress at work.
normal.cn: 谈到工作压力时，记住固定搭配 relieve the pressure。

abstract.en: Picture a valve turning loose and steam hissing out of a blocked pipe.
abstract.cn: 想象一个阀门被拧松，蒸汽从堵塞的管道里嘶嘶冒出。

abstract.en: Imagine handing a heavy suitcase to a friend at the top of the stairs.
abstract.cn: 想象在楼梯顶端把沉重的行李箱交给朋友。

abstract.en: See two guards saluting as one walks away and the other steps into place.
abstract.cn: 想象两名卫兵敬礼，一个走开，另一个站到岗位上。

examples.en: These tablets should relieve the swelling within a day.
examples.cn: 这些药片应该在一天之内缓解肿胀。

examples.en: I was relieved to hear that everyone was safe.
examples.cn: 听说大家都平安，我松了一口气。

examples.en: A new team will relieve the workers at midnight.
examples.cn: 一支新的队伍将在午夜替换这些工人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞丽舞」——想象瑞丽的舞蹈让紧绷的人放松下来；只是谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 古法语 relever，源自拉丁语 relevare（re-「再次」+ levare「举起」，levis「轻」），核心为「把重量抬起」。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses are versions of the same act of lifting: lifting pain, lifting a duty, lifting a burden, lifting dullness.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都是同一个「抬起」动作的不同版本：抬起疼痛、抬起职责、抬起负担、抬起沉闷。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tight valve loosened so that pressure falls.
core.cn: 核心意象：拧紧的阀门被松开，压力随之下降。

branches.en: Loosening pressure is felt first as less pain.
branches.cn: 松开压力最先被感受为疼痛变轻。

branches.en: Lifting a duty off one person puts it on another, which is the relieving shift.
branches.cn: 把职责从一人身上卸下交给另一人，就是接替。

branches.en: Taking a heavy thing out of someone's hands is the sense of freeing.
branches.cn: 把重物从某人手里拿走，就是使其摆脱。

branches.en: A dull stretch is pressure too, so a change relieves it.
branches.cn: 沉闷的时段也是一种压力，变化正是在缓解它。

branches.en: All three come from the same movement of weight leaving a person.
branches.cn: 前三项都来自重量离开同一个人的同一个动作。

intro.en: Relieve keeps the Latin prefix, the Latin root, and a French verb ending in one short word.
intro.cn: relieve 在短短一个词里保留了拉丁前缀、拉丁词根和法语动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin re- adds the idea of back or again, and levare supplies the lifting, so the verb means to lift back up.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 带来「回、再」的意思，levare 提供「举起」，合起来就是「重新抬起」。

items.example: Re- appears again in remove and renew.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 也出现在 remove 与 renew 中。

items.example: The lev- root also lifts in lever.
items.exampleCN: lev- 词根在 lever 中也表示抬起。

items.example: Levare supplies the second half of relieve.
items.exampleCN: levare 提供 relieve 的后半部分。

items.meaningCN: 标记动词不定式形式的词尾
items.example: The final -e comes from the French infinitive relever.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -e 来自法语不定式 relever。

items.example: Relevare is the direct ancestor of relever.
items.exampleCN: relevare 是 relever 的直接来源。

items.meaning: the easing of pain or worry
items.example: Relief drops the verb ending and keeps the same root.
items.exampleCN: relief 去掉动词词尾，保留同一词根。

items.meaning: a bar used to lift or move something
items.example: Lever is the lev- root in its plainest lifting form.
items.exampleCN: lever 是 lev- 词根最直白的「抬起」形式。

items.meaning: to raise to a higher position
items.example: Elevate adds e- to the same lev- root.
items.exampleCN: elevate 在同一个 lev- 词根前加了 e-。

definition_zh: 宗教；宗教信仰；执着的追求
definition_en: belief in a god or gods, and the system of worship and moral rules that goes with it
core_image: 一条把人反复系回神圣之物的绳索
scene: 每天做早饭之前，外婆都会在小神龛前点香、合掌。Every morning before cooking, my grandmother practices her religion at the small altar.
sceneCN: 这里 religion 是「宗教」（第 2 个义项：一套信仰与仪式体系）；句意：每天做饭前，外婆都会在小神龛前进行她的宗教活动。

pos.zh: 宗教；宗教信仰；执着的追求

derivatives.zh: religion 加 -ous 构成，义为「宗教的；虔诚的」
religious 加 -ly 构成，义为「虔诚地；一丝不苟地」

senses.title: Belief in a divine power
senses.definition: the belief that a god or gods exist and that people should worship them
senses.definitionCN: 相信存在神并应当对其崇拜的信念
senses.example: Religion gave the villagers comfort after the earthquake.
senses.exampleCN: 地震之后，宗教信仰给了村民们安慰。
senses.why: If the old root means to bind, then religion is the cord that ties a person to the divine.
senses.whyCN: 如果古老的词根意为「系紧」，那么宗教就是把人与神明系在一起的那根绳索。

senses.title: A system of faith and worship
senses.definition: one of the organized systems of faith, ritual, and moral teaching followed by a group
senses.definitionCN: 一群人遵循的、由信仰、仪式与道德教义组成的有组织体系
senses.example: Buddhism is one of the great religions of Asia.
senses.exampleCN: 佛教是亚洲的伟大宗教之一。
senses.why: A single binding cord becomes a shared framework when a whole community is tied by the same beliefs and rites.
senses.whyCN: 当整个群体被同一套信仰与仪式系在一起，那一根绳索就变成了一套共同体系。

senses.title: Something pursued with devotion
senses.definition: an activity that someone treats with the seriousness and devotion normally given to a faith
senses.definitionCN: 某人以近乎信仰的认真与投入对待的活动
senses.example: For him, fitness is a religion rather than a hobby.
senses.exampleCN: 对他而言，健身不是爱好，而是一种信仰。
senses.why: The binding force of faith can be transferred to any practice that rules a person's days, hence the figurative use.
senses.whyCN: 信仰那种系住人的力量可以转移到任何支配日常生活的活动上，于是有了这个比喻用法。

intro.en: The origin of religion is debated. Most reference works point to Latin religare, to bind fast, while others argue for relegere, to read over again.
intro.cn: religion 的词源存在争议：多数辞书认为来自拉丁语 religare「系紧」，也有学者主张来自 relegere「反复阅读、重新重视」。

items.en: Religare combines re- with ligare, to bind, and means to tie fast.
items.cn: religare 由 re- 与 ligare「捆绑」组合，意为牢牢系住。

items.en: Relegere means to read over again or to go over carefully, and is the rival explanation.
items.cn: relegere 意为反复阅读或仔细重温，是另一种解释的来源。

items.en: Religio in classical Latin covers scruple, reverence, and the fear of the gods.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语 religio 涵盖顾忌、敬畏以及对神明的畏惧。

items.en: Old French religion names a monastic order as well as a system of faith.
items.cn: 古法语 religion 既指修会，也指信仰体系。

items.en: English adopts religion for a system of faith and for the state of being devout.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪引入 religion，指信仰体系与虔诚的状态。

items.en: The modern word keeps the system sense and adds the playful sense of a devoted pursuit.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「体系」之义，并增添了「执着追求」这一戏谑用法。

note.en: Religion sits beside words for belief, and it looks like several Latin words built on the same re- prefix.
note.cn: religion 与表示「信念」的词相邻，外形上也与若干由 re- 开头的拉丁词相近。

entries.definition: relating to religion or believing strongly in it
entries.definitionCN: 宗教的；虔诚的，由 religion 加 -ous 构成

entries.definition: in a very regular and careful way
to bind together, a rare technical verb
entries.definitionCN: 捆扎；系紧，是罕见的技术用词，与 religion 共享 ligare 词根

entries.definition: strong belief in a religion or in someone
entries.definitionCN: 信仰；信任，侧重内心的确信

entries.definition: a feeling that something is true or real
entries.definitionCN: 信念；看法，范围比 religion 更宽

entries.definition: a formal statement of religious belief
entries.definitionCN: 信条；教义，是宗教信念的正式表述

normalIntro.en: The word is usually explained through Latin ligare, to bind, so most hooks use the image of a tie.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词通常用拉丁语 ligare「捆绑」来解释，所以记忆钩子多用「系住」的画面。

normal.en: Religion and ligament share the lig- root of binding; one ties a person to a faith.
normal.cn: religion 与 ligament 共享表示「捆绑」的 lig- 词根，一个系住人，一个系住骨。

normal.en: The adjective religious adds -ous, and the adverb religiously adds -ly after that.
normal.cn: 形容词 religious 加了 -ous，副词 religiously 再在其后加 -ly。

normal.en: Religiously also means doing something very regularly, as if it were a ritual.
normal.cn: religiously 还表示极为规律地做某事，像是在行仪式。

normal.en: Freedom of religion is a fixed phrase worth learning as one block.
normal.cn: freedom of religion 是值得整块记住的固定表达。

normal.en: Remember that the binding explanation is the usual one but not the only hypothesis.
normal.cn: 记住「捆绑」是通行解释，但并非唯一假说。

abstract.en: Picture a rope looped around a person and tied to a high stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子绕过一个人，系在高处的石头上。

abstract.en: See a whole village kneeling in the same direction at dawn.
abstract.cn: 想象黎明时整个村庄朝同一个方向跪拜。

abstract.en: Think of a runner who treats a morning run like a sacred duty.
abstract.cn: 想一位把晨跑当成神圣义务的跑者。

examples.en: Religion has shaped the art and music of this region.
examples.cn: 宗教塑造了这个地区的艺术与音乐。

examples.en: The law protects freedom of religion for every citizen.
examples.cn: 法律保护每位公民的宗教信仰自由。

examples.en: He follows his religion with great care.
examples.cn: 他非常认真地奉行自己的宗教。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞丽珍」——想象把珍视的信念系在身上；只是谐音联想，与真实词源无关。

root: 一般认为来自拉丁语 religare（re-「牢牢地」+ ligare「捆绑」），另有 relegere（反复阅读）一说，词源存争议。

sensesIntro.en: From one binding cord come the personal belief, the organized system, and the devotion given to anything at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一根系紧的绳索，长出个人的信仰、有组织的体系，以及对任何事物的执着投入。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope tying a person back to something sacred.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条把人与神圣之物系在一起的绳索。

branches.en: The tie is felt first as personal belief.
branches.cn: 这根绳索最先被感受为个人的信仰。

branches.en: When a community shares the tie, it becomes an organized system.
branches.cn: 当整个群体共享这根绳索，它就成为有组织的体系。

branches.en: The same binding force can grip a hobby, giving the figurative sense.
branches.cn: 同样的系缚之力也能抓住一项爱好，产生比喻义。

branches.en: Personal belief and shared system are two scales of the same bond.
branches.cn: 个人信仰与共同体系是同一种纽带的两个尺度。

branches.en: Both a church and a cherished routine rule the order of a day.
branches.cn: 教会与珍视的日常习惯都支配着一天的秩序。

intro.en: Religion is a Latin noun with a prefix, a root, and a suffix, all carried into English through French.
intro.cn: religion 是一个拉丁名词，含前缀、词根与词尾，经法语进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Latin re- strengthens the action, ligare means to bind, and -io names the resulting state.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 加强动作，ligare 表示「捆绑」，词尾 -io 表示由此形成的状态。

items.example: Re- tightens the action in religare.
items.exampleCN: 在 religare 中，前缀 re- 加强了动作。

items.example: The lig- root also binds in ligament.
items.exampleCN: lig- 词根在 ligament 中也表示系缚。

items.example: Ligare is the verb behind the lig- root.
items.exampleCN: ligare 是 lig- 词根背后的动词。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The ending -io turns the verb into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -io 把动词变成表示状态的名词。

items.example: Religare is the usual source given for religion.
items.exampleCN: religare 是 religion 通常被追溯到的来源。

items.example: Religio already carries both fear and worship.
items.exampleCN: religio 同时带有畏惧与崇拜两层意思。

items.meaning: a band of tissue that ties bones together
items.example: Ligament keeps the binding sense of ligare.
items.exampleCN: ligament 保留了 ligare 的「系缚」含义。

items.meaning: a duty that ties a person to an action
items.example: Obligation adds ob- to the same ligare root.
items.exampleCN: obligation 在同一个 ligare 词根前加了 ob-。

definition_zh: 宗教的；虔诚的；一丝不苟的
definition_en: connected with religion, or believing strongly in a religion
core_image: 每天同一时刻点灯、同一方向叩拜的人
scene: 寺院的钟声一响，山下的居民就放下手里的活，走进那座古老的建筑。When the temple bell rang, the villagers stopped their work and walked into the old religious building.
sceneCN: 这里 religious 是「宗教的」（第 1 个义项：与宗教有关的）；句意：寺院的钟声一响，村民们停下手里的活，走进那座古老的宗教建筑。

pos.zh: 宗教的；虔诚的；一丝不苟的

derivatives.zh: religious 加 -ly 构成，义为「虔诚地；一丝不苟地」
religious 的名词来源，义为「宗教」
加否定前缀 ir- 构成，义为「不虔诚的；无宗教信仰的」

senses.title: Connected with religion
senses.definition: relating to religion, its beliefs, or its practices
senses.definitionCN: 与宗教、其信仰或仪式有关的
senses.example: The building is used for religious ceremonies.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑用于宗教仪式。
senses.why: The adjective is simply the noun religion with a Latin ending added, so it describes anything that belongs to that binding system.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是名词 religion 加上拉丁词尾，因此描述一切属于那套系缚体系的东西。

senses.title: Believing strongly in a faith
senses.definition: believing firmly in a religion and taking part in its practices regularly
senses.definitionCN: 坚定地信仰某种宗教并规律参与其仪式
senses.example: Her grandmother was a deeply religious woman.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖母是一位非常虔诚的女性。
senses.why: A person held tightly by the bond of faith is described with the same adjective, which shifts from belonging to devotion.
senses.whyCN: 被信仰之绳牢牢系住的人也用同一个形容词描述，词义从「属于」转向「虔诚」。

senses.title: Done with great care and regularity
senses.definition: done carefully and at fixed times, as if it were a duty
senses.definitionCN: 认真且按固定时间去做，仿佛是一项义务
senses.example: He checks the figures with religious care.
senses.exampleCN: 他以近乎虔诚的仔细核对数字。
senses.why: Someone who never misses a rite becomes the model for anyone who never misses a routine.
senses.whyCN: 从不缺席仪式的人，成了从不漏掉任何例行事务之人的范本。

intro.en: Religious is the Latin-derived adjective of religion, formed with the ending -ous.
intro.cn: religious 是由 religion 派生、带拉丁词尾 -ous 的形容词。

items.en: Religiosus describes someone careful about rites and full of scruple.
items.cn: religiosus 形容对仪式谨慎、心存顾忌的人。

items.en: The suffix -osus means full of, so religiosus means full of religious care.
items.cn: 词尾 -osus 表示「充满」，因此 religiosus 意为「满怀宗教式谨慎的」。

items.en: Old French religieus keeps both the belonging sense and the devout sense.
items.cn: 古法语 religieus 同时保留「属于宗教」与「虔诚」两层意思。

items.en: English religious first names members of a monastic order.
items.cn: 英语中的 religious 最初指修会成员。

items.en: The adjective widens to cover anything connected with faith and, figuratively, any careful routine.
items.cn: 这个形容词后来扩展到一切与信仰有关的事物，并比喻性地指任何谨慎的例行做法。

note.en: Religious is the everyday adjective of the religion family, and it stands near words for devotion and for belief.
note.cn: religious 是 religion 词族中日常使用的形容词，并与表示虔诚和信念的词相邻。

entries.definition: belief in a god or gods and its system of worship
entries.definitionCN: 宗教；宗教信仰，是 religious 的名词来源

entries.definition: in a very careful and regular way
entries.definitionCN: 虔诚地；一丝不苟地，由 religious 加 -ly 构成

entries.definition: showing no interest in or respect for religion
entries.definitionCN: 不虔诚的；漠视宗教的，由否定前缀 ir- 构成

entries.definition: very religious and sincere in belief
entries.definitionCN: 虔诚的，语气比 religious 更强

entries.definition: showing deep respect for God and religion
entries.definitionCN: 虔诚的；恭敬的，有时带做作之意

entries.definition: relating to the human spirit rather than the body
entries.definitionCN: 精神的；心灵的，不必然属于宗教

normalIntro.en: Religious is just religion plus the Latin ending -ous, so the hooks mostly revisit the noun.
normalIntro.cn: religious 就是 religion 加上拉丁词尾 -ous，所以记忆钩子大多回到那个名词。

normal.en: Drop the noun ending and add -ous: religion becomes religious.
normal.cn: 去掉名词词尾，加上 -ous，religion 就变成 religious。

normal.en: Add -ly and you get religiously, which also means doing something without fail.
normal.cn: 再加 -ly 得到 religiously，它也表示从不间断地做某事。

normal.en: Add the negative prefix ir- for irreligious, the opposite of devout.
normal.cn: 加否定前缀 ir- 得到 irreligious，与虔诚相反。

normal.en: Deeply religious is a very common pairing in both speech and writing.
normal.cn: deeply religious 是口语和书面语中都很常见的搭配。

normal.en: The family also contains religion and religiosity, all built on the same root.
normal.cn: 这个词族还包括 religion 和 religiosity，都建立在同一词根上。

abstract.en: Picture a person who lights the same lamp at the same hour every day.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人每天同一时刻点亮同一盏灯。

abstract.en: See hands folded and eyes lowered in a quiet room.
abstract.cn: 想象安静的房间里合起的手与低垂的眼。

abstract.en: Think of someone checking a list three times, as if it were a rite.
abstract.cn: 想一个人把清单核对三遍，仿佛在行仪式。

examples.en: The festival has both a religious and a social side.
examples.cn: 这个节日既有宗教的一面，也有社交的一面。

examples.en: She comes from a very religious family.
examples.cn: 她来自一个非常虔诚的家庭。

examples.en: He follows the training plan with religious discipline.
examples.cn: 他以近乎虔诚的自律执行训练计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞丽哲思」——想象瑞丽小城里有人整日哲思信仰；只是谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 religiosus（对仪式谨慎、心存敬畏），源自 religio；词尾 -osus 表示「充满」。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective starts as a label for things belonging to faith and widens to describe a devout person and then any careful routine.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词起初标记属于信仰的事物，随后扩展到形容虔诚的人，再扩展到任何一丝不苟的例行做法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person who keeps the same rite at the same hour.
core.cn: 核心意象：每天同一时刻行同一仪式的人。

branches.en: Anything tied to the faith is labelled with the adjective.
branches.cn: 一切与信仰相关的事物都用这个形容词标记。

branches.en: A person held by the bond is called devout rather than merely belonging.
branches.cn: 被这根绳索系住的人，就从「属于」转为「虔诚」。

branches.en: Never missing a rite becomes the model for never missing a routine.
branches.cn: 从不缺席仪式，成为从不漏掉例行事务的范本。

branches.en: The belonging sense and the devout sense grow from the same root.
branches.cn: 「属于宗教」与「虔诚」两义出自同一词根。

branches.en: Both stress regularity in the service of something held sacred.
branches.cn: 两者都强调为某种被视为神圣之物而保持的规律性。

intro.en: Religious keeps the Latin root of religion and adds an adjective ending.
intro.cn: religious 保留 religion 的拉丁词根，并加上形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The ending -osus means full of, so religiosus describes a person full of religious care.
latinIntro.cn: 词尾 -osus 表示「充满」，因此 religiosus 形容满怀宗教式谨慎的人。

items.example: The relig- root is shared with religion.
items.exampleCN: relig- 词根与 religion 共用。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The ending -ous turns a noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 把名词变成形容词。

items.example: Religiously adds -ly to the adjective.
items.exampleCN: religiously 在形容词后加了 -ly。

items.example: Irreligious uses ir- before the letter r.
items.exampleCN: irreligious 在字母 r 前使用 ir-。

items.example: Religiosus is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: religiosus 是直接的拉丁来源。

items.example: Religio supplies the stem of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: religio 提供这个形容词的词干。

items.example: Religiosity adds -ity to the same stem.
items.exampleCN: religiosity 在同一词干后加了 -ity。

items.meaning: connected with God and treated with great respect
items.example: Sacred is a near partner of religious in meaning.
items.exampleCN: sacred 在语义上是 religious 的近邻。
